Order 
This criminal revision under section 397 read with section 401 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 is preferred challenging the legality of judgment dated 5.9.2018 passed in criminal appeal No.138/2018 by the Additional Sessions Judge, Rajgarh arising out of judgment dated 09.01.2018 in criminal case No.420/2016 by the J.M.F.C., Khilchipur, District Rajgarh (M.P.) whereby respondents/accused persons have been acquitted from charges under sections 498-A, 323/34 and 506(Part-II) of the IPC in a case arsing out of crime No.233/2016 registered at P.S.-Khilchipur, District Rajgarh.
2. Facts of the case in brief are that revision petitioner was married to respondent no.1 Kamlesh on 10.05.2015 as per hindu rituals.
Respondent no.2 Prem Singh is father-in-law and Respondent no.3 is mother-in-law and Respondent no.4 is sister-in-law of the revision petitioner.

3. Crime No.233/2016 was registered against respondents on NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29427 2 CRR-5119-2018 14.07.2016 at P.S. Khilchipur District-Rajgarh.

The case was registered on a written complaint (Exhibit-P/1) submitted by revision petitioner before P.S.-
Susner on 02.07.2016 and recorded at P.S. Susner District- Agar Malwa at 0/16 and forwarded to P.S. Khilchipur District-Rajgarh through Superintendent of Police, Rajgarh.
The allegations were made that she is being harassed for unlawful demand of dowry.
She was being physically assaulted and threat to kill the life was extended through physically as well as through phone.
Cylinder of LPG was kept open so that physical harm be caused to the revision petitioner.
After investigation, final report was submitted and charges were framed under sections 498-A, 323/34 and 506(Part-II) of the IPC.

4. Respondents abjured the guilt and to bring home the guilt the prosecution has examined revision Smita vs Kamlesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147308930/
1 petitioner as PW-1, her mother Narmada Bai as PW-2, her father Bansilal as PW-3 head constable Bhupendra Saxena posted at Police Station- Khilchipur as PW-4, Indrajeet Singh posted at Police Station - Susner as PW-5.
5. In examination under section 313 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 all the facts and circumstances were either denied or ignorance was expressed except the fact that marriage was solemnized on 10.05.2015.

Their defense was false implication.
6.
Appreciating the evidence the trial court acquitted the respondents/accused from all charges.

7. Revision petitioner preferred an appeal under the proviso of 372 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 vide judgment dated 05.09.2018 in criminal appeal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29427 3 CRR-5119-2018 no.138/2014 was dismissed.

sentences.text: 8. Challenging the acquittal of the respondents by the trial court as well as appellate court this revision petition is preferred on the ground that both the courts below recorded perverse findings and she was not subjected to cruelty or physical assault and threat to life was not extended.

9. Heard.
10.

Counsel for the respondents oppose the criminal revision and submitted that concurrent finding of facts recorded by the trial court as well as appellate court are based on proper appreciating of evidence.
No case for interference in the limited scope of revision is made out.
Acquitting by both the courts cannot be disturbed in this revision petition.

11. Perused the record.
12.

Revision petitioner (PW-1) was assistant teacher posted at village pagariya under the Govt. H.S.
School Nalkheda Sankul.
She has admitted in para-22 of her deposition that she was living in her maternal home since 11.02.2016.

In para-22 of the judgment of the appellate court there is detailed discussion regarding the explanation in not lodging the report from 11.02.2016 to 02.07.2016 and the explanation that she want to save the relationship have been found in contradiction with the testimony of his father Banshilal PW-3 who have admitted that his daughter have decided on 11.02.20216 that she will not return to matrimonial home.

Appellate court has decided in para-25 of the testimony of the victim that she was not ready to participate in the marriage function of her sister-in-law and she did not attend the marriage function of her sister-in-law.
Trial court has considered NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29427 4 CRR-5119-2018 para-5 of victim (PW-1) that her husband was trying to resolve the dispute by mutual understanding.

Trial court and appellate court has rightly noticed the inconsistency in the testimony of victim (PW-1) and her mother (PW-2) and father (PW-3) regarding demand of dowry, physical assault and incident of leaking LPG.
Findings are not perverse hence, no interference is called for.
Accordingly this criminal revision is dismissed.
(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE ajit Smita vs Kamlesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147308930/
